Hamlaneh · chat shell · quiet nest
Chat shell
Nine artboards plus the component sheet, on the tokens already in webapp/src/tokens.css. Messages are bubbles — grouped runs under one avatar, own messages on the logical end side, so the Persian mirror swaps sides rather than merely re-aligning text. The live shell below is a working chat-default: switch channels, send a message, open search, toggle theme and language.

chat-components
what this set adds to Quiet Nest · geometry, message anatomy, states, behaviour, bidi
01 · geometry
Three permanent regions, one optional fourth
No new colour, type or spacing tokens — everything below is composed from webapp/src/tokens.css. The four sizes this set does add are region widths, listed on the right.
org header 64
Sidebar
280 fixed
user footer 60
channel header 64
Message list — fills, scrolls
bubble max-width 520
composer — grows to 120 max
Search results
340, conditional
sidebar width280
search panel width340
bubble max-width520
mobile drawer width300
header / footer height64 / 60
sidebar row / drawer row36 / 44
message list padding18 / 28
Desktop rows are 36 px tall because the pointer is precise and density matters in a list read all day; on mobile every row and control goes to 44 px. Both clear the 40 px product floor for touch, since the 36 px desktop row is pointer-only.
02 · message
Bubble anatomy and grouping
Others' messages sit on the logical start side in surface with a border.subtle outline; your own sit on the logical end side in brand.soft with no outline. The first bubble of a run notches its leading top corner to 4 px; the rest stay at 12 px. Side is set by align-items on a column flex, so RTL mirrors with no extra rules.

03 · sidebar
Row states, presence, badges
read · secondary text
hover · neutral tint
active · brand.soft
unread · bold + outline count4
mention · filled + @@2
private · lock replaces hash
keyboard focus
Unread is weight plus an outlined count; a mention is a filled brand badge carrying an @. Fill, glyph and weight all differ, so the two never rely on colour to be told apart.
Presence — shape, not just colour
Nonline · solid
Oaway · barred
Poffline · hollow
Every dot also carries a text presence label in the DM header and the user footer, so the state is never dot-only.
Avatar tints
N O P A
Four token fills only — brand.primary, accent.warm, info, success — assigned by a stable hash of the user id, all carrying on-brand text. Initials are the fallback when no photo is uploaded.

05 · behaviour
Interaction, accessibility, bidi, responsive
Messaging
Enter sends, Shift+Enter opens a line. The hint row states this permanently rather than teaching it once.
A sent message appears immediately as your own bubble; failure to reach the server converts it to the dashed queued treatment rather than dropping it.
Consecutive messages from one author within five minutes group under a single avatar, name and timestamp.
The unread divider is placed on entry and stays until you leave the channel — it does not jump as new messages arrive.
Editing replaces the bubble with an inline composer; the message keeps its position.
Deleting leaves a dashed placeholder so the conversation does not silently reshape.
Accessibility
The message list is a labelled log region; new arrivals announce politely, never assertively.
Connection changes announce through role="status"; nothing steals focus from the composer.
Hover actions are reachable by keyboard: focus inside a message reveals the same toolbar.
Bubble fill is never the only carrier of authorship — the name row and the side both say it, and both survive high-contrast mode.
Every avatar has a text name beside or behind it; presence dots pair with words.
Desktop rows are 36 px pointer targets; every touch target is 44 px.
Bidi
Bubble side comes from align-items on a column flex, so the whole conversation mirrors from the dir attribute alone.
Corner notches use border-start-start-radius / -start-end-radius, never top-left or top-right.
Channel slugs, filenames, version tags and URLs are isolated LTR runs inside Persian text.
Message bodies are dir="auto" — a Persian message in an English workspace still reads correctly.
Only directional glyphs mirror: send, reply and back. Attach, search, download and the hash do not.
Persian sets at 1.7–1.75 line-height with no negative tracking.
Responsive
1440
1024
375
≥ 1280 — as drawn; the search panel opens as a third column.
900–1279 — desktop shell; search becomes an overlay above the message list instead of a third column.
≤ 899 — full mobile shell at the 375 reference: sidebar becomes a 300 px drawer over a scrim, opened from the header.
375 — 56 px top bar, 44 px controls, bubble max-width 264, one-line markdown hint, safe-area padding under the composer. Tauri chrome never overlaps the top bar.
Component tree
ChatShell
├ Sidebar
│ ├ OrgHeader
│ ├ ChannelList → ChannelRow
│ ├ DmList → DmRow
│ │ └ PresenceDot
│ └ CurrentUserFooter
├ ChannelHeader
│ └ SearchInput
├ MessageList
│ ├ DaySeparator
│ ├ UnreadDivider
│ ├ MessageGroup → MessageBubble
│ │ ├ MessageActions
│ │ ├ FileCard · ImageCard
│ │ └ LinkPreviewCard
│ └ HistoryLoader
├ Composer
│ └ MarkdownHintRow
├ ConnectionBanner
└ SearchResultsPanel → SearchResult
Reused from the auth set without change
Every colour, type step, spacing value, radius, focus ring, disabled treatment and motion duration. The dashed-boundary disabled convention carries over from the login fields to the disconnected composer. Banner anatomy — icon plus text, tinted fill, 1 px matching border — is the same component as the login notices, with warning and success reused for connection state.
New icons this set needs
hash · lock · users · search · paperclip · send · pencil · trash-2 · link · file-text · image · download · menu · shield · settings · ellipsis-vertical · wifi-off — all Lucide, same 24 × 24 viewBox at 1.75 stroke as the auth set. Nothing here is drawn outside that family.
chat-addendum-create-channel-light
modal over chat-default · Public selected · the visibility note is persistent, never a tooltip

chat-addendum-overlay-components
anatomy · geometry · variant matrix in both themes · layering · locale keys · behaviour
01 · geometry
Three overlays, no new tokens
Every value below already exists in webapp/src/tokens.css or in the delivered chat set. The scrim is the same text.primary at 42% the mobile drawer uses; elevation is the existing overlay step.
create-channel dialog560 wide
people picker520 × 616
people picker (Persian, 3 rows)520 × 470
mention popover380 wide, max-height 268
dialog radius / popover radius14 / 12
person row min-height56
mention row min-height48
row action pill34 high in a 56 row
scrimtext.primary @ 42%
popover offset above composer116 from board bottom
Layering and dismissal
The two dialogs sit at z-index 4 over a z-index 3 scrim, exactly as the mobile drawer does. The mention popover has no scrim and does not trap focus — it is a popover, not a dialog.
Escape, Cancel, the close control, or a backdrop press closes a dialog. Focus returns to the invoker: the Channels + for create-channel, the DM + or the channel action for the picker.
Escape closes the mention popover and leaves the caret exactly where it was. Tab closes it and follows normal focus order — it never inserts on Tab.
The popover is clamped to the viewport and capped in height; long lists scroll inside it.
02 · variants
Every state in both themes
Light and dark are the same geometry with mapped tokens. No state is carried by colour alone: focus adds a 3px ring, busy adds a spinner and a dashed boundary, the active mention row adds weight and an inline-start bar.

Hover tints the row; the keyboard-active descendant additionally gains weight, an inline-start bar and the Enter hint, so pointer and keyboard state never look the same.
03 · behaviour
What an implementer must not guess
Create channel
Submitted payload is exactly a slug and a kind. No topic, description, members or discoverability — not hidden, absent.
Slug is 2–64 characters matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$, always an isolated LTR run including inside Persian UI.
The visible # prefix is decoration and is not part of the submitted value.
Initial focus enters the name field. The primary action is disabled while empty, invalid or submitting, and cannot fire twice.
Invalid and duplicate names are field-level errors announced beside the input; a request failure is a banner and preserves both the name and the kind.
The busy label sits in a fixed-width button so Creating… cannot resize it.
Neither kind is browsable in this release. No copy anywhere implies find, browse, join or read access.
People picker
One component, two modes: invite into the open channel, newDm to open or reuse a one-to-one. Single-pick and immediate in both.
The whole row is one semantic button with no nested control. Accessible name: Invite Nasrin Ahmadi, @nasrin, to #deploys / Message Nasrin Ahmadi, @nasrin.
A row shows only initials avatar, display name, complete @username and optional presence. No email, role, team or photo.
There is no reliable already-a-member signal in the current data contract, so none is drawn.
Only the activated row goes busy; the rest stay live. Success closes the dialog; failure keeps the query and results and offers recovery.
More results load progressively from a cursor. No numbered pagination.
Refreshes announce politely; load and action failures announce assertively without stealing focus.
Mentions — required behaviour, not a reskin
The picker opens from an @ typed at the current composer token and from the existing Mention someone control. Both paths are the same component.
This @-query behaviour is a product requirement of this addendum, not a visual change to an existing feature.
Editable combobox over a listbox with aria-activedescendant. Focus never leaves the composer.
Arrow Up/Down moves the active row, Enter inserts, Escape closes, Left/Right keep moving the caret, Tab closes and moves on without inserting.
Filtering is client-side over the already-loaded channel member list. No new server search endpoint is implied.
The stored reference is <@{user_id}>. The UI renders the display name and never shows the UUID or the raw token.
Sent-message mention styling is deliberately not designed here — that open question stays open.
04 · locale keys
New strings needing matching en and fa keys
Everything else on these artboards is existing delivered copy, reused verbatim.
channel.error.invalidSlugUse 2–64 lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores.
channel.error.duplicateThat channel name is already in use.
channel.action.submittingCreating…
people.state.loadingLoading people…
people.state.noResultsNo people found.
people.state.directoryEmptyNo one else is available.
people.error.loadPeople could not be loaded. Try again.
common.action.retryTry again
people.action.invitingInviting…
people.action.openingOpening…
mention.list.labelMention a channel member
mention.state.loadingLoading members…
mention.state.noMatchNo matching members.
mention.error.loadMembers could not be loaded. Try again.
Persian UI uses ASCII digits 0–9 for every app-generated number — times, dates, unread and member counts, badges, file sizes, counters and limits. User-authored messages, topics, filenames, usernames and technical strings stay exactly as authored.
05 · rtl & narrow
Mirroring and 375
Logical mirroring
The Persian picker is the same component with dir="rtl". No row-reverse, no DOM reordering, no transform of a finished LTR layout.
Avatar and presence sit at logical inline-start — the right in RTL. Identity text follows. The row action sits at logical inline-end — the left.
All alignment is text-align: start; all spacing is padding-inline / inset-inline.
Display names are dir="auto" runs, so Omid Rezaei stays Latin inside a Persian list — user-owned names are never translated.
Complete @usernames and #slugs are isolated LTR runs. Isolation is semantic; no invisible bidi controls go into translation strings.
Search, close, avatar and person icons do not mirror. Only genuinely directional arrows do.
DOM, reading and keyboard order stay logical and are never reversed to imitate the visual order.
At 375 inside chat-mobile
Both dialogs become full-bleed sheets with a 16px inline gutter and the existing safe-area padding — no new breakpoint is introduced.
The people picker keeps its header and search pinned; only the result list scrolls, so the search field never goes out of reach behind the keyboard.
Row actions stay at logical inline-end at 44px; the row itself is the target, so it grows rather than the pill.
The mention popover anchors above the composer and is clamped to the viewport, shrinking its cap rather than overflowing.
Focus rings are never clipped: no ancestor of a focusable element in these overlays uses overflow:hidden without room for the 3px ring and 2px offset.
Acceptance
Normal text ≥ 4.5:1; meaningful controls and icons ≥ 3:1 against the surface behind them, verified in both themes.
Every interactive element keeps the existing 3px ring at 2px offset.
Dialogs are labelled by their visible headings; the composed name adds the channel where it applies.
Search keeps a visible label — the placeholder is supplementary.
Loading indicators occupy reserved space so nothing shifts when results land.
Errors sit beside the control or action they concern and always carry a recovery path.
Avatars are decorative: the same row already names the person in text.
Layout survives 200% zoom and text scaling.

chat-addendum-menu-components
anatomy · anchors and collision · layering · focus and keyboard · locked corrections · locale keys
01 · model
Anchored non-modal dialogs, not ARIA menus
Both surfaces hold something a menu cannot: Channel actions contains a form, Account contains a radio group. So both are role="dialog" with aria-modal="false", and their triggers carry aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-expanded and aria-controls. No menu, no menuitem, no roving tabindex, no arrow-key menu navigation, no page scrim, no desktop focus trap.
channel popover344 wide
account popover292 wide
mobile channel popoverinset-inline 10, fluid
mobile account popover280 wide, inside the drawer
popover radius12
anchor gap from trigger12
internal padding12–16
row / control height44
close control44 × 44
max height100% of region minus 24, then scrolls
elevationexisting overlay step
scrimnone on desktop; the drawer’s own on mobile
Anchors and collision
Channel actions anchors below the header ellipsis at logical inline-end, offset 12. Account anchors above the identity trigger at logical inline-start, offset 12.
Each popover is clamped to its owning region and to the viewport. When space is short it shifts along the cross axis first, then caps its height and scrolls internally — it never clips content and never introduces horizontal scrolling.
The mobile account popover is clamped inside the 300 px drawer as well as the viewport.
Opening any other top-level chat surface closes the current popover first. Only the topmost transient surface answers Escape.
Language switching moves the complete anchored pair — trigger and popover — to the opposite logical side without animating across the viewport. Direction changes atomically.
02 · focus & keyboard
Normal DOM order, restored on dismissal
Entry and dismissal
Channel actions: focus enters Topic. Account: focus enters Close.
Tab and Shift+Tab follow DOM order. Channel actions: Close, Invite people, Topic, Save topic. Account: Close, Change password, language radiogroup, Log out.
Escape and the visible Close dismiss and restore focus to the trigger.
An outside activation dismisses and leaves focus on the chosen outside target — focus is never pulled backward.
If Tab leaves both the popover and its trigger, the popover dismisses without reclaiming focus.
The language radiogroup keeps native semantics: the checked radio is the single tab stop and arrow keys move between EN and فا. Arrows never traverse the other account actions.
Topic contract
Maximum 250. Empty deliberately clears the topic, and the helper says so.
The authored value is preserved exactly — never trimmed, translated, normalised or reshaped.
Save is disabled while the draft equals the current topic; returning to the exact original restores the pristine state. A changed empty value is valid and enables Save.
Over 250 is a field-level error that disables Save. The counter is ASCII, aria-live="off", and does not announce per keystroke.
Enter submits when valid and idle. Duplicate submission is impossible.
Saving uses a stable-width Saving…, marks the form busy and does not shift the popover.
Success updates the header topic, closes, restores focus, and announces Topic saved. politely. Failure keeps the popover open, preserves the exact draft, restores the controls and allows retry; editing clears the stale error. Closing mid-request does not cancel the update.
Dirty drafts and logout
A dirty topic is never discarded silently. Close, Escape, an outside activation, a channel switch, reactivating the trigger, or choosing Invite people all turn the same anchored surface into the discard confirmation.
Keep editing restores the editor and focuses Topic. Discard changes completes the originally requested destination. Escape from the confirmation means Keep editing.
The confirmation uses hierarchy and copy, never accent red — this system reserves red controls for message deletion.
Invite people is an ordinary button: it closes this popover, opens the existing invite-mode people picker and moves focus to that dialog’s search field. Cancelling the picker returns focus to Channel actions.
Log out is neutral, unconfirmed and duplicate-safe, with a stable-width Logging out…. There is deliberately no logout error state — the local session clears even if the server request fails.
03 · triggers
What changed in the shell
Two corrections to the delivered chat set, both visible on the primary artboards.
Channel actions trigger
The existing header ellipsis becomes the trigger, named Channel actions.
It renders only for an active public or private channel. In a DM and in the no-channel state it is absent from the DOM — not disabled, and never a popover that exists only to say nothing is available.
The mobile build currently hides it entirely. Corrected: a 44 × 44 trigger sits beside search in the mobile header, clear of the title, the drawer control and the search affordance.
The desktop trigger also grows from the delivered 34 × 34 to 44 × 44 so it clears the product floor. The ten earlier chat artboards still show the pre-correction 34 px ellipsis — they are the historical record, and this sheet is the value to build.
Public and private channels have identical permissions and identical actions. Only the hash or lock treatment distinguishes them. Nothing implies that a public channel can be found, browsed, joined or read by a non-member.
Account trigger — placeholder wiring resolved
The placeholder code opened Account from the Settings gear. That predates the delivered Settings panel.
Final structure: the avatar, display name and presence block is one 44 px-tall disclosure button named Open account menu. The adjacent gear stays a separate Settings button that opens the delivered Settings panel directly, and the Admin control stays separate where applicable.
Settings and Admin are never nested inside the identity button, and there is no redundant Settings row inside the Account popover.
Change password closes the popover and enters the same voluntary change flow the Settings Security panel already owns. No second password form is designed here.
04 · locked corrections
Superseding earlier annotations on this canvas
Responsive tiers
≥ 1280 — desktop shell; search may occupy the third column.
900–1279 — desktop shell; search becomes an overlay.
≤ 899 — full mobile shell at the 375 reference.
There is no separate 1024 behaviour. The earlier 1024 row on chat-components has been corrected to this set.
Numerals
Persian UI uses ASCII digits 0–9 for every app-generated number: times, dates, unread and member counts, badges, file sizes, counters and limits.
Generated numbers are never shaped into Persian digits. User-authored messages, topics, filenames, usernames and technical strings stay exactly as authored.
The previous "digit policy unresolved" annotation has been removed from this canvas.
The Persian limit string keeps its numerals exactly: موضوع باید 250 نویسه یا کمتر باشد.
Rendered mentions
Thanks @Ava — pushing the canary now.
Thanks @Ava — pushing the canary now.
Semantic mapping — brand.hoverlight #194941 · dark #9ADACF
A rendered mention is inline text in the existing brand tone at weight 500. No pill, chip, background, border or rounded container.
Weight plus tone carries the distinction, so it survives greyscale and high-contrast mode.
The token is brand.hover in both themes — #194941 light, #9ADACF dark. The light value is never hardcoded into dark mode. brand.primary is tuned for large text and chrome, so body-size accent text uses the hover step.
This resolves the open question the earlier addendum deliberately left alone.
05 · handoff
Variants and locale keys
Reusable variants
ChannelActionsTrigger(active=true|false)active=false renders nothing at all — the element is absent, not disabled.
ChannelActionsPopover(kind=public|private, entry=header|setTopic, state=pristine|dirty|saving|error|discardConfirm)entry=setTopic opens with Topic focused and selected; entry=header opens with the caret at the end.
TopicEditor(value=empty|filled|overLimit, state=pristine|dirty|saving|error)Owns the counter, the 250 limit, the empty-clears contract and Enter-to-submit.
AccountTrigger(state=closed|open, dir=ltr|rtl)open tints with brand.soft and flips the chevron. Never wraps Settings or Admin.
AccountPopover(theme=light|dark, dir=ltr|rtl, language=en|fa)Geometry is identical across all eight combinations.
AccountAction(kind=default|logout, state=default|hover|pressed|focus|busy)logout differs only by spatial separation and label — no danger colour.
LanguageSwitcher(language=en|fa)Reused unchanged from the auth set. Native radios, fill plus weight, no flags.
Localization — every string in both addendaKeys map into the repository’s existing chat.* namespace — no competing namespace is introduced. Numerals inside strings stay ASCII in both languages, including the Persian 250 and 2–64.

RTL mirroring
Genuine dir="rtl" with logical properties. No row-reverse, no DOM reordering, no transform of the finished LTR surface. Centred dialogs use inset-inline:0; margin-inline:auto with a vertical-only transform, never a physical X translation.
Anchors move to logical start/end; Close stays at logical inline-end; headings, labels, helper text and actions all use text-align: start.
The complete channel slug renders as one isolated LTR unit — <bdi dir="ltr">#deploys</bdi> — so it never reads as deploys#. Topic and display-name content are dir="auto". EN is an isolated LTR run; فا keeps its own script direction.
Hash, lock, user-plus, ellipsis, close, settings and loader icons do not mirror.
Logical DOM, reading, focus and keyboard order are preserved and never reversed to imitate the visual order.
Vazirmatn at the existing Persian line-height with no negative tracking.
Motion, live regions and acceptance
Only the existing durations: feedback within 100 ms, state transitions 180 ms, nothing over 300 ms. Opacity and transform only.
prefers-reduced-motion drops to a single-frame opacity swap; the popover never animates position.
Topic saved. announces through a polite status region. Save failure is an alert beside the topic action and does not steal focus. The counter is aria-live="off".
Every interactive target is at least 44 × 44. Focus is the existing 3 px ring at 2 px offset and is never clipped.
No state depends on colour alone: selected language adds weight and fill, disabled adds a dashed boundary, busy adds a spinner, errors add an icon and text.
Light and dark geometry is identical. Layout survives 200 % zoom and text scaling in portrait and landscape.
06 · specimens & overflow
Scale, targets and column fit
Full frames are production geometry. The two state sheets are reference sheets, and their specimens are drawn at roughly 0.9× so nine to twelve states fit one row band.
Target sizes
In every full frame — desktop, RTL and mobile — each interactive element measures at least 44 × 44: the channel trigger, the account disclosure, Close, Invite people, the topic field, Save topic, both language radios and Log out.
The state-sheet specimens are non-production illustrations. Their controls are drawn at 40 px and their popovers at 300 px so a full state matrix reads in one view. Build to the full-frame geometry and the numbers in §01, never to the sheet specimens.
Each state sheet carries this note at its head as well, so a specimen can never be measured out of context.
Coverage in both themes: default, hover, pressed, keyboard focus, disabled, busy, invalid, error and confirmation. The dark column of each sheet repeats pristine, saving, error and the confirmation at identical geometry.
Column fit
Both state sheets are 1920 wide with 48 padding and a three-column grid, so each column is 586 and the widest specimen is 376 — nothing overflows horizontally.
The component sheets use the same 1920 frame. Every grid-template-columns here is a fraction-based repeat(n,1fr), never a fixed track wider than its share, so columns shrink with the frame instead of spilling.
The mention popover is clamped with max-inline-size: calc(100% - 336px) so it stays inside the chat pane clear of the 280 px sidebar.
Dialogs centre with inset-inline: 0; margin-inline: auto and a vertical-only transform — never inset-inline-start: 50% with a physical X translation, which mis-shifts under dir="rtl".
07 · mobile dismissal
Two surfaces, two scopes
Account inside the drawer
Account Close dismisses only the Account popover. The drawer stays open and focus returns to the identity trigger inside it.
Tapping the drawer scrim closes both, in one gesture — the popover first, then the drawer.
Escape closes only the topmost surface: Account first, then the drawer on a second press.
The drawer’s existing scrim is reused. Account never adds a second scrim of its own.
The Settings gear inside the drawer footer remains a direct Settings trigger and is never nested in the identity button.
At insufficient height the popover collision-shifts and scrolls internally rather than clipping.
Channel actions on mobile
A 44 × 44 trigger sits beside search in the mobile header, clear of the title and the drawer control.
Same anchored-popover family as desktop — deliberately not a bottom sheet, and with no scrim.
The editable Topic field is set at 16px computed so iOS Safari does not auto-zoom when the software keyboard opens.
The popover keeps Topic and Save above the keyboard, capping its height and scrolling internally within the available dvh.
Verified in portrait, landscape and at 200 % zoom.
08 · icons
Exact Lucide glyphs added by this addendum
All at a 24 × 24 viewBox, 1.75 stroke, currentColor, round caps and joins — the same family and weight as the delivered sets.
chevron-up · 15px in the account triggerDoes not mirror. Vertical disclosure: up means the popover opens upward.
chevron-down · 15px, collapsed triggerDoes not mirror. Swaps with chevron-up on open, never rotates in RTL.
key-round · 17px, Change passwordDoes not mirror. It reads as an object, not a direction.
log-out · 17px, Log outMirrors in RTL. Its arrow is genuinely directional — leaving points toward the logical end.
Also reused unchanged: ellipsis-vertical, hash, lock, user-plus, x, settings, loader-circle, search and paperclip. Only log-out and arrow-left mirror; every other glyph in this set stays as drawn.
